Package com.stzteam.features.advantagekitbridge

Class AdvantageKitBridge

java.lang.Object
com.stzteam.features.advantagekitbridge.AdvantageKitBridge
public final class AdvantageKitBridge extends Object
The entry point of the MARS <-> AdvantageKit bridge Feature.

One call wires every ModularSubsystem in the robot into AdvantageKit's logging and replay pipeline. No subsystem, IO interface or Data class has to change: MARS already hands each input snapshot to its global input hook right after the hardware is polled and before any Request runs, and that is precisely where AdvantageKit needs to sit for replay to be deterministic.

Quick start

The shortest path is MarsLoggedRobot, which does the whole AdvantageKit setup for you based on the MARS Environment.RunMode: 
 public class Robot extends MarsLoggedRobot {
     public Robot() {
         super(Manifest.CURRENT_MODE);
         // ... build your RobotContainer as usual
     }
 }
If you would rather drive AdvantageKit yourself, do the standard setup and then install the bridge before Logger.start(): 
 AdvantageKitBridge.install();
 Logger.start();

What gets logged

  • Every subsystem's Data snapshot, as AdvantageKit inputs, under the subsystem's name. These are what replay feeds back in.
  • MARS diagnostics (ActionStatus per subsystem, plus the active alert list), as AdvantageKit outputs. See MarsDiagnosticsLogger.

Replay

In Environment.RunMode.REPLAY the hook runs fromLog instead of toLog, overwriting the snapshot MARS is about to hand to absolutePeriodic, the active Request and the Telemetry. Everything downstream therefore sees the recorded hardware state rather than live or simulated hardware, which is what makes a replay reproduce the match. This works whether or not a Data class overrides snapshot() to return a defensive copy, because MARS passes that same snapshot to the hook.

Threading

Like Logger.processInputs itself, the bridge must only be driven from the main robot thread.

  • Method Details

    • configure

      public static void configure(BridgeConfig newConfig)
      Replaces the active configuration. Call this before install(): the per-class field plans bake in the key style, so reconfiguring drops every cached plan and any adapter already built.
      Parameters:
      newConfig - The configuration to use.

    • getConfig

      public static BridgeConfig getConfig()
      Returns:
      The active configuration, never null.

    • install

      public static void install()
      Registers the bridge with MARS core so every subsystem's inputs flow into AdvantageKit. Idempotent: calling it twice does not double-log.

      Safe to call before Logger.start() -- AdvantageKit discards input and output writes until the logger is running.

    • uninstall

      public static void uninstall()
      Removes the bridge from MARS core and drops its per-subsystem caches. Mainly useful for test isolation; a robot program has no reason to uninstall mid-match.

    • isInstalled

      public static boolean isInstalled()
      Returns:
      True if the bridge is currently forwarding inputs.

    • processInputs

      public static void processInputs(String name, Object data)
      Logs (or, during replay, restores) one data object under a table of its own. This is what the global hook calls for each subsystem, exposed so you can bring structures MARS does not own -- a vision pipeline's outputs, a co-processor's packet -- into the same replayable pipeline.
      Parameters:
      name - The table name, to which the configured inputs prefix is prepended.
      data - The object to log. Objects already implementing LoggableInputs, such as classes generated by AdvantageKit's @AutoLog processor, are passed straight through and serialise themselves.

    • recordDiagnostics

      public static void recordDiagnostics()
      Records the MARS diagnostics tree immediately. The bridge already does this once per cycle on its own; call it explicitly only if you want the statuses captured at a specific point of your loop instead.

    • configureLogger

      public static void configureLogger(com.stzteam.mars.builder.Environment.RunMode mode)
      Performs the standard AdvantageKit receiver/replay-source setup for a MARS Environment.RunMode, then records MARS and Feature versions as log metadata.

      This is the boilerplate from AdvantageKit's installation guide, expressed once:

      • Environment.RunMode.REAL: write a .wpilog to the USB stick (or to /home/lvuser/logs) and publish live to NetworkTables.
      • Environment.RunMode.SIM: publish live to NetworkTables only.
      • Environment.RunMode.REPLAY: read the log AdvantageScope selected and write the recomputed outputs beside it with a _sim suffix.
      It does not call Logger.start(), so you can add your own receivers first. It also cannot set the replay timing mode, which needs the robot instance -- use MarsLoggedRobot to get that handled too.
      Parameters:
      mode - The run mode to configure for.

    • isReplaying

      public static boolean isReplaying()
      Returns:
      True if AdvantageKit is replaying a log rather than reading live hardware. Prefer this over checking Environment.getMode() when the question is "is the logger feeding me recorded inputs right now".

    • reset

      public static void reset()
      Clears every cached field plan, adapter and warning. Intended for tests that compile the same classes repeatedly under different configurations.
